module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        current ||= snapshot

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end

steps.message: The current job has two correctness bugs: it falls back to the original snapshot when the authoritative row disappears/changes, and it uses an unconditional upsert that can replace a newer revision’s embedding. I’ll change the post-provider phase to lock and re-read the document by ID, validate tenant/publication/revision, and only then write within that transaction; an existing embedding with a greater revision will cause `:discarded`. The provider remains entirely outside the transaction, so exceptions naturally produce no write.

**Implementing atomic transaction lock**

I realize that an atomic transaction lock is essential here. I need to be careful to avoid using `find_by` with lock scope behavior like `Document.lock.find_by(id:)`. This could lead to issues I want to prevent. I should implement an alternative approach to ensure that everything functions smoothly without causing any problems. I'll figure out the best way to achieve that while keeping the transaction safe and efficient.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      # The provider is deliberately called before opening the transaction. It may be
      # slow (and may call a remote service), so neither the connection nor the row is
      # held while it runs.
      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id)
        next :discarded unless current
        next :discarded unless current.tenant_id == tenant_id
        next :discarded unless current.published?
        next :discarded unless current.revision == snapshot.revision

        existing = Embedding.lock.find_by(document_id: document_id, version: version)
        # A result for an older revision must never replace an embedding generated
        # for a newer one. The document lock serializes jobs for this document.
        next :discarded if existing && existing.revision > snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert(
          { document_id: current.id, tenant_id: current.tenant_id,
            revision: snapshot.revision, version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) },
          unique_by: %i[document_id version]
        )
        :stored
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobTest < BenchmarkTest
  def call(document, provider:)
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(document_id: document.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: provider)
  end

  def test_revision_change_during_provider_discards_result
    doc = document
    result = call(doc, provider: lambda { |_body|
      doc.update!(revision: 2)
      [1]
    })

    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_withdrawal_deletion_and_tenant_reassignment_are_discarded
    [
      ->(doc) { doc.update!(published: false) },
      ->(doc) { doc.destroy! },
      ->(doc) { doc.update!(tenant_id: 'b') }
    ].each do |change|
      doc = document
      result = call(doc, provider: lambda { |_body|
        change.call(doc)
        [1]
      })

      assert_equal :discarded, result
      assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
    end
  end

  def test_provider_error_is_propagated_without_writing
    doc = document
    error = assert_raises(RuntimeError) { call(doc, provider: ->(_body) { raise 'provider failed' }) }

    assert_equal 'provider failed', error.message
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_newer_embedding_is_not_overwritten
    doc = document
    Knowledge::Embedding.create!(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', revision: 2,
                                 version: 'v1', vector: JSON.generate([2]))

    assert_equal :discarded, call(doc, provider: ->(_body) { [1] })
    assert_equal JSON.generate([2]), Knowledge::Embedding.find_by!(document_id: doc.id, version: 'v1').vector
  end

  def test_embedding_versions_coexist
    doc = document
    job = Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new
    provider = ->(_body) { [1] }

    assert_equal :stored, job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: provider)
    assert_equal :stored, job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v2', provider: provider)
    assert_equal %w[v1 v2], Knowledge::Embedding.where(document_id: doc.id).order(:version).pluck(:version)
  end
end
